Land is a resource that can be used, but it also has an implicit cost. When using land, you are essentially giving up the opportunity to use it for another purpose. This implicit cost is often referred to as an "implicit cost" in economics. The explicit cost is the money paid for renting the land. The use of land itself, in this sense, is a cost because it represents the value of the next best alternative.
